trust_decision.summary: Untrusted CSS text (a <style> body or a style attribute) is matched by the CSS scrubber's property:value regex; the unbounded property-name quantifier lets a long name run with no colon backtrack quadratically. The fix caps the name at 64 characters in one regex.

landing_point.why: The summary names the CSS scrubber regex. It is the only Regex.replace in CSS.scrub, and css.ex is the only module named CSS.

fix_sites.entry_point: HtmlSanitizeEx.html5/1 (lib/html_sanitize_ex.ex:121) via <style> tag body (lib/html_sanitize_ex/scrubber/html5.ex:2233-2257) and style attributes (lib/html_sanitize_ex/scrubber/html5.ex:2152, lib/html_sanitize_ex/scrubber/meta.ex:206-210); also public HtmlSanitizeEx.Scrubber.CSS.scrub/1 and custom scrubbers using Meta.allow_tags_with_style_attributes (lib/html_sanitize_ex/scrubber/meta.ex:167)
fix_sites.module_kind: core library helper (CSS scrubber shared by all style routes)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: None that holds up: every route into the regex goes through the single CSS.scrub function, so a fix at css.ex:11 covers all of them at once.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Valid declarations must keep passing through unchanged (e.g. 'div.foo { width: 500px; height: 200px; }', 'font-weight: bold', long names like 'border-bottom-color'), and disallowed properties must still be stripped. A fix that drops or truncates long CSS input, or rejects names over a small cap, breaks these.

O6_input_shapes: style attribute value on allowed tags

O8b_injection_room.sibling: scrub_val token regex could be written as an unbounded value grammar (e.g. nested ([-\w]+\s*)+ for multi-word values) on the same untrusted value
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Value parsing for multi-token CSS values (font-family lists) is a natural place for a maintainer to add a richer regex; still a ReDoS route of the same concept, so a where-type extra only.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a URI scheme capture without the 20-char slice (String.slice) before the lazy .+? capture
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The slice is a separate guard line; a second URI helper (e.g. for srcset or meta content url) could plausibly omit it. Different sink, though, so it sits outside this advisory's protection.

O9_family: ReDoS (CWE-1333) quadratic regex backtracking in CSS scrubber

O10_build.toolchain: mix / Elixir 1.20.1 (per commit 97d3d4b), Erlang/OTP; dependency mochiweb

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Bound the property-name quantifier ({1,64}) or add a possessive/atomic group in the single CSS regex; that is the published fix and it closes every route.

out_of_scope_notes: lib/html_sanitize_ex/parser.ex:33-35,50-58 apply regexes to all untrusted HTML; read as linear (single quantifier between literal anchors) and not pursued.
unverified: repo_mb not measured (no shell size check); the library is small, likely under 5 MB, which would add tiny_repo.
Whether the {1,64} cap fully removes super-linear behaviour (e.g. repeated 64-char runs) was not analysed; no code was run.
O1 counts html5/1, CSS.scrub/1 and the custom-scrubber Meta macro as distinct entry points; all three reach the same single regex.
